title: Full or Lite Decision Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Analytics
Learning Record Store
LRS-Lite
Architecture Decisions
description: Describe a school by roster size, budget and requirements, see which of the Lite, single-server and Full LRS tiers each requirement rules out, and recommend the cheapest tier that still fits.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Choosing between the Full LRS, a single-server tier and LRS-Lite
learningObjectives: The learner will recommend Full, single-server or Lite for a described school by weighing scale, freshness, evidence integrity and budget, and will justify the recommendation against the trade-off table.
prerequisites: Full LRS capacity and cost model (Chapter 21)

accessibility.notes: Native p5 sliders, checkboxes and buttons; describe() is updated with the recommendation; unmet requirements use a cross symbol and text, not color alone.

keyQuestions: Which requirement rules out Lite for this school?
What is the cheapest tier that meets every requirement?
Which row of the trade-off table justifies the choice?
commonMisconceptions: That the choice is only about price
That Lite cannot serve any graded use without a server
That the single-server tier has the same resilience as Full
assessmentOpportunities: Recommend and justify for three described schools
Critique a factor the heuristic ignores

equations: A tier fails if students exceed its scale target (Lite ~150, single server ~10,000)
A tier fails if the budget is below its lowest estimate (Lite ~$1, single ~$300, Full ~$10,300)
Lite fails evidence, cross-class analytics and real-time alert requirements
Single server and Full fail without staff to run servers
Recommend the cheapest tier with no unmet requirement
assumptions: Cost and scale figures are design or planning estimates quoted in Chapters 21-23
limitations: A teaching heuristic, not an official sizing tool; ignores high availability, migration effort, licenses and engineering time
